what_its_for: Osimertinib is a targeted cancer medicine used to treat a type of lung cancer called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It works specifically in patients whose cancer has certain gene changes (mutations) in a protein called EGFR. Your doctor has tested your tumor and confirmed it has one of these mutations. This medicine blocks abnormal signals that tell cancer cells to grow and multiply.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. You can take it with or without food — whatever is easiest for your stomach. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep steady levels of the medicine in your body. If you have trouble swallowing the tablet, you may dissolve it in a small amount of plain water (about 2 tablespoons). Stir until dissolved, drink immediately, then rinse the glass with more water and drink that too. Do not crush or chew the tablet.
dosing: The usual dose is 80 mg once daily. In some cases, your doctor may prescribe 40 mg once daily, for example if you have side effects that are hard to manage. Always take the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor or pharmacist first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and your next scheduled dose is MORE than 12 hours away, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If your next dose is LESS than 12 hours away, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store your tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture and heat — do not store in a bathroom or near a stove. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking St. John's Wort (a herbal supplement) as it can make osimertinib less effective. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, because many medications can interact with osimertinib. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine — it can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 weeks (females) or 4 months (males) after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking osimertinib.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden new or worsening shortness of breath, cough, or fever (possible lung inflammation called interstitial lung disease or pneumonitis); chest pain, fast or irregular heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting (possible heart rhythm problem called QTc prolongation); sudden vision changes or eye pain (possible eye problems); skin rash, blistering, or peeling; signs of a blood clot such as swelling, redness, or pain in your legs; or any signs of infection. Also contact your doctor if you have prolonged nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or any side effects that are bothering you.
when_it_works: Osimertinib starts working at the cellular level right away, but it may take several weeks before you or your doctor notice visible changes. Some patients feel better within a few weeks, while for others it may take a couple of months for imaging scans to show tumor shrinkage. Keep taking your medicine every day even if you feel well, and do not stop without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use during pregnancy. Use reliable birth control. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Older adults (65+): No special dose adjustment is needed, but watch closely for side effects. Kidney or liver problems: If you have moderate to severe liver problems, your doctor may adjust your dose. Remind your doctor of any kidney or liver conditions before starting treatment. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
